record.paper_title: Research Problems on Relations Between Nijenhuis Geometry and Integrable Systems
record.original_question: Is Frobenius structure itself projectively invariant, and can the flat metric in the definition of a Frobenius structure be replaced by a metric of constant curvature?

evidence.quote: Problem 6.3. Certain Frobenius manifolds seem to give examples of geometric Poisson bracket of order 3 ... Is Frobenius structure projectively invariant? Can one replace, in the definition of Frobenius structure, the flat metric by a metric of constant curvature?

artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as a research problem in the context of Nijenhuis geometry and integrable systems. A web search did not surface a published resolution stating either that Frobenius structures are projectively invariant or that the flat metric can be replaced by a metric of constant curvature; related works on flat pencils of metrics in Frobenius manifolds and on metric projective structures exist but do not address this specific equivalence. The problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Flat pencils of metrics and Frobenius manifolds
status_evidence.snippet: Any Frobenius manifold carries a natural quasihomogeneous linear pencil of metrics that form a flat pencil.
status_evidence.claim: Standard Frobenius manifold theory uses a flat metric and produces a flat pencil of metrics; replacing flatness by constant curvature is not addressed.

status_evidence.title: Projectively related metrics, Weyl nullity, and metric projectively invariant equations
status_evidence.snippet: Studies metric projective structures and projectively invariant equations; does not establish projective invariance of Frobenius structures.
status_evidence.claim: No known result asserts projective invariance of the full Frobenius structure.
